title: Adaptive quantization-aware kernel scheduler for prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dequantization overhead and suboptimal kernel choice for INT8/FP8 mixed-precision paths is a dominant component of prefill latency at small to medium batch sizes. Current kernel selection heuristics pick kernels based on static model-wide heuristics (layer type and global precision), which misses per-request sequence length skew and cache-friendliness, resulting in avoidable epilogue copies and KV cache churn.

Proposal: Implement an adaptive kernel scheduler that: (1) scores candidate kernels per-layer using a latency+memory cost model that includes dequantization epilogue cost, (2) incorporates recent per-tenant sequence length histograms and microbatching profile to choose mixed-precision execution (e.g., prefilling in INT8 with FP8 attention epilogue vs FP16 for long-sequence windows), and (3) applies a lazy dequantization window on decode to defer full-cast until token emission if possible. The scheduler will expose a small runtime policy surface for SLOs: tail latency budget, token throughput target, and quality budget (expected numeric noise).

Key technical ideas: 
- Per-layer cost model: static kernel benchmark matrix (shapes, strides) + dynamic modifiers (seq_len, microbatch_size, kv-cache hit rate).
- Fused int8-epilogue kernels: add a kernel path which accepts packed INT8 tensor + per-channel scale metadata to emit attention results without an intermediate fp32 buffer. This eliminates one epilogue copy for many common heads.
- Lazy dequant window: for decode, maintain small INT8 KV cache and only dequantize active head slices needed for the next N tokens; full dequant happens opportunistically on idle GPU cycles or when a fallback occurs.
- Fallback policy: fall back to FP16 kernels when the scheduler predicts >1.5% expected QA degradation or when dequant memory + kernel scheduling would exceed the latency SLO.

Why different from current work: existing tickets focus on kernel fusion and general prefilling scheduling but do not combine per-tenant sequence histograms + lazy dequantization + a scoring layer that selects mixed-precision per-layer per-request. This ticket is explicitly about the runtime decision surface and integration with the KV cache lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive scheduler implemented and hooked into runtime kernel selection API
Fused INT8 epilogue kernel implemented for attention (no intermediate fp32 copy) and validated against numeric baselines
End-to-end e2e benchmark showing >=10% median prefill latency reduction and >=15% throughput increase for typical small-batch chat workloads vs baseline on recommended models
A rollout plan with canary checkbox and fallback to current kernel selection when quality or latency regressions are detected
Documentation (console + SDK) for the runtime policy knobs and observability metrics added
comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after perf review with SRE. Observed 24% median prefill speedup gap when comparing ideal fused path vs our current epilogue pattern.

2026-02-27 Liam Chen: Spike complete. Microbench results: fused int8 epilogue reduces epilogue copy cost by ~35% for common head dims (64, 128). Sample harness: /bench/fused-epilogue/2026-02-26.tsv (internal).

2026-03-03 Design review: UX agreed on two knobs - tail_latency_budget_ms and quality_budget_pct. Console graph will show per-model kernel decisions. Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/QUANT-SCHED-2026 (internal).
2026-03-08 PR opened for kernel scorer and policy hooks: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1442 - waiting CI and perf regression jobs.

2026-03-10 Performance update: Canary run on staging (10% traffic) shows median prefill -12%, p95 -9% for small-batch chat; decode tail latency unchanged. Observed rare quality diffs in top-k sampling for one customer prompt set; investigating with quality monitoring team.
metrics: Baseline median prefill latency (small-batch chat): 82.3 ms
Canary median prefill latency (with scheduler): 72.4 ms
Memory reduction (hot KV working set): ~28% measured on g4dn-equivalent nodes
decision: Implement staged rollout: (1) land kernel scorer + observability flags behind a feature flag, (2) ship fused int8 epilogue kernel with unit/regression tests, (3) enable lazy dequant window for decode behind per-customer policy, (4) monitor quality metrics for 2 weeks before enabling globally.
